english.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔文武百官就第赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。
english.before: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
english.after: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. He was posthumously granted the honorary rank Kaifu Yitong Sansi (Opening an Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies) and the post of Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
english.reason: The source title is 開府儀同三司. 'Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal' renders a different prestige title, 金紫光祿大夫, as in 18 of the 21 Jiu Tangshu units that use 'Golden Seal'. The replacement uses the same Kaifu Yitong Sansi form as extraction claim-304 and keeps the rest of the sentence.

english.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔文武百官就第赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。
english.before: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. By edict he was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
english.after: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. By edict he was posthumously granted the titles Opening an Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies (Kaifu Yitong Sansi) and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
english.reason: Same mistranslation as the idiomatic field: 開府儀同三司 is not 金紫光祿大夫. The literal replacement translates 開府 (open an office), 儀同 (ceremonial equal to) and 三司 (the Three Excellencies) and keeps the transliteration.

english.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。
english.before: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.
english.after: In the third year his father Desheng was also posthumously granted the title Prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.
english.reason: 追贈…為魏州刺史 confers an office posthumously; 刺史 is a prefectural post, not a fief, so 'enfeoffed' is a mistranslation. The replacement also restores 又 ('also'), which marks this as a further favor after Li Yifu's own promotions in s0166-s0167.

english.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。
english.before: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.
english.after: In the third year his father Desheng was further posthumously granted the office of Prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.

english.zh: 如意元年，則天以義府與許敬宗、御史大夫崔義玄、中書舍人王德儉、大理正侯善業、大理丞袁公瑜等六人，在永徽中有翊贊之功，追贈義府揚州大都督，義玄益州大都督，德儉魏州刺史，公瑜江州刺史。
english.before: In 692 Empress Zetian, because Yifu together with Xu Jingzong, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yixuan, Palace Secretariat Drafter Wang Dejian, Senior Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Hou Shanye, and Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu—the six men who during the Yonghui era had rendered meritorious support—posthumously enfeoffed Yifu as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, Yixuan as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou, Dejian as Prefect of Weizhou, and Gongyu as Prefect of Jiangzhou.
english.after: In 692, because Yifu, together with Xu Jingzong, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yixuan, Palace Secretariat Drafter Wang Dejian, Senior Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Hou Shanye, and Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu—six men in all—had rendered meritorious support during the Yonghui era, Empress Zetian posthumously granted Yifu the title Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, Yixuan Area Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou, Dejian Prefect of Weizhou, and Gongyu Prefect of Jiangzhou.
english.reason: 追贈 confers posthumous offices (大都督, 刺史), not fiefs, so 'enfeoffed' is a mistranslation. The before text also leaves the 'because' clause (以…有翊贊之功) without a finite verb, because 'had rendered' sits inside the parenthetical. The replacement keeps all six names and all four grants exactly as in the source.
